title: Your first app with Meta's AI

source.title: Quickstart, Meta Model API docs
source.creator: Meta
source.licence: Meta's own documentation, credited; steps written fresh

goal.sentence: Build a small app that asks Meta's AI a question and prints its answer.

files.README.txt:
Your first app with Meta's AI

Your Meta key is already in this terminal's settings, under the name META_API_KEY.
Your code reads it from there with os.environ["META_API_KEY"].
Never paste the key itself into a file: anyone who sees the file could use it.

steps.instruction: On line 1, type from openai import OpenAI and save.
steps.why: Meta's quickstart uses the openai package to talk to its models.
hints: A package is code someone else wrote that you can use.
from a package import a name brings that name into your file.
Type from openai import OpenAI on line 1.

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: OpenAI lives inside the openai package. Write from openai import OpenAI
Not yet: the package is spelled openai, with no underscore.

steps.instruction: On line 3, make a client for Meta, then save.
steps.why: base_url sends your questions to Meta instead of to OpenAI.

args.text:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1")

hints: A client is the object that sends your questions.
OpenAI( ) makes one; base_url says where it sends them.

args.text:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://api.meta.ai/v1")

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: the address starts with https, with an s: https://api.meta.ai/v1

steps.instruction: Give the client your key from META_API_KEY, then save.
steps.why: Code gets shared; a key read from the setting stays private.

args.text:
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["META_API_KEY"])

hints: Your key is already stored in a setting named META_API_KEY.
Add import os on line 1: os.environ reads settings.

args.text:
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1", api_key="made-up-key-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv")

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: never paste the key. Read it with os.environ["META_API_KEY"]

args.text:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1", api_key="META_API_KEY")

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: "META_API_KEY" in quotes is only the name. Use os.environ["META_API_KEY"]

steps.instruction: Ask muse-spark-1.3 a question with client.responses.create, then save.
steps.why: create sends your question to Meta's model and brings back its answer.

args.text: response = client.responses.create(model="muse-spark-1.3", input="Give me one tip for learning to code.")

hints: client.responses.create( ) sends a question and returns the answer.
Give it model="muse-spark-1.3", and your question as input=
Type response = client.responses.create(model="muse-spark-1.3", input="Give me one tip for learning to code.") on line 5.

args.text: response = client.responses.creat(model="muse-spark-1.3", input="Give me one tip for learning to code.")

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: you wrote creat. Spell it create, with an e at the end.
Not yet: create needs brackets to run, with model= and input= inside.

steps.instruction: On line 6, add print(response.output_text) and save.
steps.why: output_text holds the model's reply as plain text.
hints: print( ) shows it in the terminal.

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: Python reads capitals exactly. Write print with a small p.
Not yet: print needs brackets: print(response.output_text)

steps.instruction: Run ask.py and read Meta's answer in the terminal.
steps.why: This is the moment your program talks to a real AI model.
hints: Save the file first, then run it.
Click the Run button at the top right of the editor.
Or type python ask.py in the terminal and press Enter.
